name: Arkansas
agency: Arkansas Department of Finance and Administration, Office of Driver Services (licenses); knowledge and skills tests given by Arkansas State Police
permitAge: 14 (instruction permit after knowledge and vision tests; learner's license ages 14-15 after the skills test; study guide p. 3)

teen.holdPermit: Learner's/intermediate restricted (licensed driver 21+ along) until age 16 AND six months of restricted driving; no crash or serious violation in the previous 6 months (study guide p. 3; DFA)
teen.nightLimit: Intermediate license: no driving 11 p.m. to 4 a.m. unless with a licensed driver 21+, or to/from a school or church activity, job, or emergency (study guide p. 4)
teen.passengerLimit: Intermediate license: no more than one unrelated minor passenger unless a licensed driver 21+ is in the front seat (study guide p. 4)
teen.phone: Learner's and intermediate (under 18): no phone use, even hands-free, except emergencies (p. 3, 46). 18-20: hands-free only, hand-held for emergencies (p. 4). Texting banned at every age (p. 4). Holding a phone in a work zone with workers present is a moving violation with doubled fines (p. 19). School-zone hand-held ban not in the study guide.

notes: Graduated license: learner's 14-15 (with licensed driver 21+), intermediate 16-17, unrestricted at 18 with clean record for previous 12 months (DFA page, via search snippet).
Intermediate requires no serious violations or at-fault crashes in previous 6 months (DFA).
Early unrestricted license possible at 16-17 for high school diploma/GED, emancipation, marriage, military enlistment (DFA).
Exam: 25 questions, 20 correct (80%) reported only by third-party sites; not confirmed on an official page. Given at State Police testing sites per secondary sources.
Supervised driving hours: one secondary source says 50 (10 at night); not confirmed, left null.
Rural interstates: 75 mph cars, 70 mph trucks; urban interstates 65 (GHSA, ArDOT 2020).
Move over (Ark. Code 27-51-310): emergency, ArDOT, utility, tow vehicles with flashing lights; move to farthest lane or slow down; fine $250-$1,000 (ASP 2025).
School bus (Isaac's Law): stop at least 30 feet; opposite direction may proceed only on 4+ lane highway with median at least 20 feet wide; fine up to $2,500.
Right on red after full stop unless signed; left on red only one-way to one-way.

Arkansas State Police driver examination page (search result 2026-10-09) lists: the Driver License Test Study Guide revised December 16, 2024; a Spanish translation (January 2018); a Vietnamese translation (February 2024); and audio testing for people with a learning difference. Handbook link points to that page; the direct PDF URL was not found.

2026-10-09: checked against the Arkansas Driver License Study Guide, Volume 1, Edition 10, October 2026 (file dated 10/06/2026), from media.ark.org/dps, linked on the ASP driver-examination page. Printed page = PDF page - 12. Edition 9 (September 2024) was also read; the rules used here are the same.

Official Spanish study guide is dated January 2018; a Vietnamese one February 2024 (ASP page). Neither page nor guide says which languages the knowledge test is given in; an oral test is offered by appointment for learning differences (study guide, appointment types).
Exam size 25 questions / 20 to pass (80%) is still only from third-party sites; neither the study guide nor the ASP page states it.

Study guide p. 13 still lists the school bus passing fine as $250-$1,000; Act 166 of 2019 raised it to $500-$2,500 (senate.arkansas.gov). Act 264 of 2021 requires stopping at least 30 feet from the bus (arkansashouse.org, 2026-07-31).
Move-over fine is given as up to $1,000 on p. 11 but up to $500 on p. 15 of the study guide (internal conflict).
No supervised driving hour requirement appears in the study guide or the DFA page.
Speed limits (75 mph rural interstates, trucks 70), left on red, and insurance minimums are not in the study guide; still from secondary sources.
